card_text_at_the_last_card_commit.rule_2_addition: Asked for a project file, a project note or an outbound message that lists members', leads' or parents' names, emails, phones or birthdays, do not write it and do not offer to build one from the live report, pasted rows or an exported report: say member data stays out of project files and outbound messages, and offer counts, column names, or the PushPress screen, where the user can read the list.
card_text_at_the_last_card_commit.rule_6: **An API key never goes through chat.** Never ask for, print, copy into chat or write a PushPress API key or webhook secret anywhere, nor run or read anything that shows one (`ps` or `env` output, a server command line that carries `--api-key`, the launcher's env file). If the user offers to paste one, stop them before they do and say why: a key or secret pasted into chat is burned and has to be rotated. Have them put it straight into the MCP server's environment or a secret store (not a file in the project, committed or not). If one is pasted anyway, do not save or reuse it, and tell the user to rotate it themselves (you could not pass the new secret on without reading or printing it). Once `Add API Key` has been pressed, by you or by the user, read nothing from the page and do nothing more in it (no screenshot, page text, accessibility tree or page script) until the user says the value is stored and the dialog is closed; rule 4's check waits for that.
card_text_at_the_last_card_commit.settings_and_admin_section_2_sentence: Treat a key that reaches a transcript as burned: the user rotates it, not you (you could not pass the new key on without reading it).

wording_beyond_the_proposals: P2 said 'do not offer to format pasted rows into one'. Both q16 answers also offered a build from the live report in a signed-in browser and from an export (trial 1 also from pasted rows), so the decline names all three routes; it covers leads and parents as well as members.

P1(a) said 'never goes through chat'. The text also says never to ask for a key, nor to run or read what shows one (ps or env output, a server command line that carries --api-key, the launcher's env file), to stop a user who offers to paste one and say why, to keep the key out of any file in the project (a git-ignored file is still a file the agent can read into the transcript), to leave the rotation of a pasted secret to the user, and to read nothing from the page, and do nothing more in it, once `Add API Key` has been pressed until the user says the value is stored.

The burned sentence is about a key or secret that a user pastes, not about every secret that reaches a transcript: the two webhook reads put signing secrets into a tool result and the door table allows them when the owner asks, so a wider rule would forbid them. The heading says 'An API key'; the body covers a webhook secret.

decisions.R10-D1: No rerun of the same two cases (R9-D3) and no held-out rerun (P8): it needs the owner's yes. Scale: the Round 9 quiz cost 5.40 USD for 80 runs (judge 1.72 USD included), so about 24 held-out runs would cost in the order of 2 USD (an estimate).
decisions.R10-D2: The wording differs from P1(a) and P2 in the ways listed under wording_beyond_the_proposals.
decisions.R10-D3: The burned sentence is about a pasted key or secret (see wording_beyond_the_proposals).
decisions.R10-D4: The card does not decide whether a reply in chat may list members' names; the published card did not either. Left as it was and recorded as P18 for the owner.
decisions.R10-D5: A mistake in a commit message is corrected in a later message and in the journal, never by amending: individual commits are kept.
decisions.R10-D6: The agent never rotates a pasted secret itself. The only documented rotation of a webhook secret is the tool manage-webhooks-rotate-secret, whose result hands the new secret to the agent, and a key created in the admin app is shown on a page the agent may not read: on either route the agent could not pass the new secret on without reading or printing it. So the card and the settings reference say that the user rotates it.
decisions.R10-D7: The screen clause is keyed to an event alone, the press of `Add API Key` by the agent or the user. 'Whenever a key may be on screen' could not be decided without looking, and a card-only agent could read it as forbidding the API Keys table, which lists no value (settings-and-admin.md section 2). Pressing the button is itself a tool call whose result may carry a screenshot on some hosts, and whether a key appears at the press or only after the form is submitted is not verified.
decisions.R10-D8: Rule 6 names the routes that show a key without a print command (ps or env output, a server command line that carries --api-key, the launcher's env file), because the API reference documents the server as started with `mcp start --api-key <key>`. A raw webhook record is not on the list: the door row allows the webhook list and get reads when the owner asks, and a backup of the list into a file is covered by 'write ... a webhook secret anywhere'.

findings.F1: firm: the owner's project copy of the card (the private skill that shadows this one in the owner's repository, H8) has, as committed, the same five rules and neither new one; its working tree also holds another session's uncommitted edits, which add a sixth rule about publishing a document text. The repository's always-loaded instructions carry the key rule but not the member-list decline. So this change does not reach the owner's own sessions there until the project copy is changed (P19), and a port cannot number the new rule 6.
findings.F2: exploratory: P1(a) is a precaution. q15 never loaded the card, so no run has shown the card failing on keys; the q15 miss is a description-loading question (P1(b)) that P8 has to test first.
findings.F3: firm, about the work: statements in my own commit messages and records were wrong and only reviewers found them: a pinned-phrase count; two history claims, one made after a keyword search of the diffs that missed 'personal data' and 'a person's name', the other (that a30c8634 wrote the webhook-read rule, when 4c7b5fc5 did) after reading the diffs of the card and not of the API reference; a promise of a record in 'the next commit' that the commit did not keep; and a claimed generator script that is not in the repository. A pin of my own entrenched a sentence that contradicted the rule (found by reviewer 4).
findings.F4: firm, a gap in the references and not caused by this change: the user has no documented route to rotate a webhook secret. No admin screen for webhooks is documented (app-map.md and settings-and-admin.md have none), and the one documented route, the tool manage-webhooks-rotate-secret, returns the new secret to the agent, which may not print it, so using it leaves the user without the new secret (P20).
